hypothesis: If the nits of lice, fleas and bedbugs generate nothing further, the public life-cycle accounts of those three insects will not state that the eggs hatch into a nymph or larva.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Three Wayback snapshots of CDC DPDx pages (pediculosis, fleas, bedbugs), taken because the live cdc.gov URLs returned HTTP 403, must each contain a sentence about eggs or nits that says they do not hatch, do not develop further, or produce nothing. All three pages must say that, and each page must still be about the named parasite (lice or Pediculus; fleas or Siphonaptera; bed bugs or Cimex).
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Refutes if any one of the three pages has a sentence about eggs or nits that states they hatch or give rise to a nymph or larva, and that sentence does not negate the hatching. Supports only if all three pages affirm that the eggs produce nothing further. Inconclusive with reason data-unavailable if fewer than one page can be fetched or none of the fetched pages states the fate of the egg. A single clear hatching statement refutes the universal claim even if another page is unclear.

test_contract.expected_observation: Each of the three life-cycle accounts says the eggs or nits do not develop into a later stage.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Any of the three accounts says the eggs hatch into nymphs or larvae.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Official CDC DPDx life-cycle pages for head or body lice, fleas, and bed bugs, or a dated Wayback snapshot of those same URLs when the live host refuses the download. The pages are identification and life-cycle references, independent of Aristotle.
test_contract.inference_method: Sentence coding after HTML is reduced to text. A hatching sentence is one that mentions egg or nit and hatch, nymph, or larva, without a negation in that sentence. A sterile sentence is one that mentions egg or nit and an explicit denial of further development. Negation in the same sentence beats a hatch word. The universal quantifier ('all ... generate nothing') fails if any taxon is coded as hatching.

interpretation: Aristotle's nits are the eggs of lice, fleas and bugs. 'Generate nothing' means those eggs do not give rise to a further stage of the same animal. Hatching into a nymph is the disconfirming observation. The test does not measure hatch rate, only whether the official life-cycle account states that hatching occurs.
caveats: Live CDC URLs returned HTTP 403 to this client. The Wayback availability API supplied the snapshot URLs and timestamps. The snapshot bodies were not downloaded.
A life-cycle page is a curated account, not a count of hatched eggs. The verdict is about those accounts.
